institutions.name: Ireland Strategic Investment Fund (ISIF)
institutions.aka: ISIF; managed by the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA)
institutions.strategy_fit: Ireland's sovereign development fund, which commits to external funds and managers but under a mandate requiring an Irish economic-impact footprint, tempering its use of purely global public-equity managers.
institutions.description: ISIF is Ireland's sovereign investment fund, managed by the NTMA, with total resources in the region of EUR 15 billion (about USD 16 billion) as of 2024 across a discretionary portfolio and directed holdings. It invests in and alongside external managers and funds, but its statutory mandate emphasizes investment that supports Irish economic activity and employment. It is a strategic, impact-oriented allocator.
institutions.outreach_rationale: ISIF does allocate to external managers and funds, so it is a plausible contact, but its Ireland-linked economic-impact requirement limits fit for a pure global-equity boutique without an Irish nexus. Best pursued if an Irish angle can be credibly established.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the ISIF/NTMA investment team; be prepared to articulate an Irish economic-impact rationale.
institutions.tier_reason: Allocates externally but the domestic-impact mandate makes it a difficult near-term fit for an unaffiliated global manager.
sources: Ireland Strategic Investment Fund — https://isif.ie/
institutions.region: Europe — UK, Switzerland, Germany, France & rest

institutions.name: Caisse des Dépôts (CDC)
institutions.aka: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; Groupe Caisse des Dépôts
institutions.strategy_fit: France's public long-term investor and financial group, which manages its very large financial portfolios predominantly in-house with a strong domestic and strategic orientation.
institutions.description: Caisse des Dépôts is a state-owned public financial group managing regulated savings, pension schemes and strategic investments, with a group balance sheet well in excess of EUR 1 trillion. Its financial-asset portfolios are managed largely internally by its own asset-management and long-term investment teams, with a pronounced French and European focus. External appointments are limited and typically specialist.
institutions.outreach_rationale: Included as France's flagship institutional investor, but its in-house, domestically-oriented model offers little near-term room for an external global-equity boutique. Engagement is a long-term, relationship-building exercise.
institutions.access_notes: Predominantly in-house with a public-policy mandate; treat as low-probability for external mandates. Precise externally-relevant AUM is not cleanly comparable, hence left null.
institutions.tier_reason: In-house, domestically-focused public investor with minimal external-manager appetite, making it aspirational.
sources: Caisse des Dépôts — https://www.caissedesdepots.fr/
institutions.region: Europe — UK, Switzerland, Germany, France & rest

institutions.name: New York City Retirement Systems
institutions.aka: NYCRS; Bureau of Asset Management (NYC Comptroller)
institutions.strategy_fit: The five NYC pension systems maintain a public-equity emerging-manager program administered by the Comptroller's Bureau of Asset Management, aligning with an emerging active-equity boutique.
institutions.description: The New York City Retirement Systems comprise five funds (NYCERS, TRS, BERS, Police and Fire) with combined assets of roughly $285 billion, managed with advice from the NYC Comptroller's Bureau of Asset Management. The systems have run emerging-manager allocations in U.S. and international public equity, historically deployed through managers-of-managers such as Leading Edge, Progress and Xponance. Manager selection is heavily consultant- and board-governed.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A very large external allocator with an explicit public-equity emerging-manager track record and formal manager-of-managers channels that can accommodate a newer firm. Global-equity sleeves make non-U.S. domiciled managers potentially eligible.
institutions.access_notes: Engage through the emerging-manager platform sub-advisors and the general/asset-class consultants; direct mandates are approved by individual system boards and are process-intensive.
institutions.tier_reason: Documented public-equity emerging-manager program with established sub-advisor channels, though board and consultant governance lengthens the cycle.
sources: New York City Retirement Systems / Bureau of Asset Management — https://comptroller.nyc.gov/services/financial-matters/pension/asset-management/
Office of the New York City Comptroller — Pension — https://comptroller.nyc.gov/services/financial-matters/pension/

institutions.name: New York State Common Retirement Fund
institutions.strategy_fit: Runs a long-standing multi-asset Emerging Manager Program with dedicated public-equity and fixed-income sleeves executed through program partners and separately managed accounts.
institutions.description: The New York State Common Retirement Fund, sole-trustee managed by the State Comptroller, is one of the largest U.S. public pensions at roughly $280 billion. It has committed about $9.5 billion cumulatively to its Emerging Manager Program across asset classes and works with roughly nine program partners who conduct due diligence and deploy capital into emerging managers. The Fund appointed a dedicated Emerging Managers Director in 2024, underscoring institutional commitment.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A very large, sole-trustee fund with an established emerging-manager infrastructure and public-equity mandate that regularly onboards newer firms through program partners. Its dedicated emerging-manager leadership makes it a priority target.
institutions.access_notes: Access is typically intermediated through the Fund's emerging-manager program partners (managers-of-managers) rather than direct cold outreach; identify and approach the relevant public-equity partner platforms and the Emerging Managers Director.
institutions.tier_reason: Formal, well-funded emerging-manager program with public-markets scope and dedicated staffing, reachable through named program-partner channels.
sources: New York State Common Retirement Fund | Office of the New York State Comptroller — https://www.osc.ny.gov/common-retirement-fund
Emerging Manager Definition and Life Cycle — https://www.osc.ny.gov/common-retirement-fund/emerging-manager/emerging-manager-definition-and-life-cycle
NY State Comptroller Announces Appointment of Emerging Managers Director — https://www.osc.ny.gov/press/releases/2024/02/ny-state-comptroller-announces-appointment-emerging-managers-director

institutions.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas
institutions.strategy_fit: Runs one of the largest formal emerging-manager programs in the U.S. that explicitly includes long-only and hedge-fund public-equity strategies, a direct fit for a research-driven equities boutique.
institutions.description: TRS is the fifth-largest U.S. public pension with roughly $210 billion in assets and a long-established external-manager model across public and private markets. Its Emerging Manager Program has committed about $6.2 billion to 254 emerging managers across 438 investments, spanning private equity, real estate, energy/natural resources, infrastructure, long-only and hedge funds, and an additional $5.6 billion has gone to program graduates. TRS co-hosts a large annual TRS/ERS Emerging Manager Conference that functions as a formal on-ramp for new firms.
institutions.outreach_rationale: TRS is arguably the single most reachable large U.S. institution for an emerging public-markets manager because its emerging-manager mandate, dedicated team, and annual conference are purpose-built to source firms like this one. Its low-single-billions AUM threshold and multi-generation fund eligibility fit an emerging HK boutique.
institutions.access_notes: Approach via the dedicated Emerging Manager team and the annual TRS/ERS Emerging Manager Conference; expect the program to work partly through managers-of-managers and separately managed accounts, and note consultant/advisor gatekeepers.
institutions.tier_reason: Flagship emerging-manager program that explicitly covers public-equity long-only and hedge-fund strategies, with an institutionalized sourcing channel and modest AUM thresholds.
sources: Emerging Manager Program | Teacher Retirement System of Texas — https://trs.texas.gov/investments/teams/emerging-managers
TRS/ERS Emerging Manager Conference | Teacher Retirement System of Texas — https://trs.texas.gov/investments/trs-ers-emerging-manager-conference

Texas Teachers embraces innovation in emerging managers as program marks 20 years — Pensions & Investments — https://www.pionline.com/institutional-investors/pension-funds/feature-pi-texas-teachers-emerging-manager-program-20-years/
Teacher Retirement System of Texas — Top1000funds.com — https://www.top1000funds.com/asset_owner/teacher-retirement-system-of-texas/

institutions.name: Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois
institutions.strategy_fit: Operates a two-decade-old diverse and emerging-manager program that allocates across public equities, making it a natural early institutional backer of a research-driven equity boutique.
institutions.description: TRS Illinois had about $75.7 billion in assets as of May 31, 2025, and reports that roughly 29% of its portfolio (more than $21 billion) is managed by diverse and emerging firms. Its Emerging Manager Program, established in 2005, has committed about $11 billion across 138 investments and graduated 19 firms into the core portfolio. The system hosts an annual Opportunity Forum to source and showcase emerging and diverse managers.
institutions.outreach_rationale: One of the most active and largest diverse/emerging-manager allocators in the country, with a clear public-equity component and a formal graduation pathway to larger mandates. The annual Opportunity Forum provides a direct, institutionalized point of entry.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the diverse and emerging managers investment team and attend the Opportunity Forum; allocations often route through managers-of-managers platforms (e.g., Xponance, Bivium, Progress, Leading Edge) and the general investment consultant.
institutions.tier_reason: Large, mature emerging-manager program with an explicit public-equity sleeve, formal sourcing events, and a documented path from emerging mandate to core allocation.
sources: Emerging Manager Program | Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois — https://www.trsil.org/investments/emerging-managers
TRS Celebrates 20th Anniversary of Emerging Manager Program — https://www.trsil.org/news-and-events/TRS-Celebrates-20th-Anniversary-of-EMP
Summer 2025 Topics & Report Newsletter — https://www.trsil.org/news-and-events/Summer2025-Topics-and-Report

institutions.name: New Jersey Division of Investment
institutions.strategy_fit: Launched a dedicated Emerging Managers Program built around separately managed accounts for firms with under $5 billion firm-wide AUM, including public-markets strategies.
institutions.description: The New Jersey Division of Investment manages roughly $70 billion for the state's pension system and unveiled a formal Emerging Managers Program in 2022 that it expanded in 2025, including a 'transition' fund for graduating managers. The program is centered on SMA platforms that source, diligence and oversee allocations to emerging managers, with an eligibility threshold of less than $5 billion firm-wide AUM. It is designed to build the next generation of investment talent across asset classes.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A relatively new, actively expanding emerging-manager program with a clear sub-$5B AUM threshold that squarely fits an emerging boutique. Its SMA-based structure lowers the bar for firms without long commingled track records.
institutions.access_notes: Access runs primarily through the SMA platform providers appointed to administer the program and the State Investment Council governance; monitor the Division's RFP notices and Emerging Manager Monthly coverage.
institutions.tier_reason: Recently launched and expanding emerging-manager program with explicit AUM thresholds and an SMA on-ramp suited to newer public-markets firms.
sources: NJ Division of Investment — https://www.nj.gov/treasury/doinvest/
New Jersey's $95 Billion Pension Fund Unveils Emerging Managers Program — https://www.nj.gov/treasury/news/2022/04272022.shtml
New Jersey DOI Expands Emerging Manager Program — Emerging Manager Monthly — https://emergingmanagermonthly.com/2025/05/07/new-jersey-doi-expands-emerging-manager-program/

institutions.name: Maryland State Retirement and Pension System
institutions.strategy_fit: Its Terra Maria emerging-manager program allocates to public-equity and other managers through managers-of-managers, a well-worn channel for newer active-equity firms.
institutions.description: The Maryland State Retirement and Pension System manages roughly $68 billion and runs the Terra Maria Program, a long-standing emerging/developing-manager initiative. Terra Maria deploys capital through several managers-of-managers (historically Attucks, Bivium, Leading Edge, Progress and others) that select and oversee smaller external firms across public equity and fixed income. The program is an explicit mechanism to broaden the manager roster beyond established names.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A dedicated, named emerging-manager program with an active public-equity sleeve accessible through its managers-of-managers, making it a realistic near-term target for a smaller equities firm. The manager-of-managers structure suits firms still building an institutional track record.
institutions.access_notes: Approach the Terra Maria managers-of-managers directly rather than the plan itself; the system's investment consultant and staff oversee the overall program.
institutions.tier_reason: Established emerging-manager program with a public-equity component and clear sub-advisor access points.
sources: Maryland State Retirement and Pension System — Investments — https://www.sra.state.md.us/
Terra Maria — Developing Manager Program (Maryland SRPS) — https://www.sra.state.md.us/investments/

institutions.name: California Public Employees' Retirement System
institutions.strategy_fit: Maintains a 30-year Emerging & Diverse Manager Program that defines public-market emerging managers as firms under $5 billion AUM, though its public equity is largely internally/passively run.
institutions.description: CalPERS is the largest U.S. public pension at roughly $540 billion and has invested in emerging managers for more than 30 years, with a formal Emerging & Diverse Manager Program and a 2023 commitment of about $1 billion focused on next-generation private-markets managers. It defines public-market emerging managers as those under $5 billion AUM and private-market managers under $2 billion on first-through-third institutional funds. Much of its public equity, however, is managed internally and passively, so external active-equity capacity is comparatively limited.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A marquee reference client with an explicit emerging-manager framework and large ticket capacity if a mandate materializes. The brand value of a CalPERS relationship is significant even though near-term public-equity fit is constrained.
institutions.access_notes: The emerging-manager effort tilts toward private markets and often uses fund-of-funds/advisors; expect heavy staff and board process and specialist consultants.
institutions.tier_reason: Real emerging-manager program and huge scale, but public-equity is mostly internal/passive and the program leans private-markets, making a near-term active-equity mandate slower.
sources: Emerging & Diverse Manager Program — CalPERS — https://www.calpers.ca.gov/investments/sustainable-investments-program/emerging-diverse-manager-program
CalPERS Emerging Managers Fact Sheet — https://www.calpers.ca.gov/documents/emerging-managers-fact-sheet-pdf/download

institutions.name: California State Teachers' Retirement System
institutions.strategy_fit: Runs an emerging-manager effort within its 'Diversity in the Management of Investments' program that includes equity platforms, and it retains external active-equity managers.
institutions.description: CalSTRS is the second-largest U.S. public pension, with assets in the region of $360 billion (recent figures range up to the low-$400s billion). Its Diversity in the Management of Investments program supports emerging managers, including woman- and minority-owned firms, with outstanding emerging-manager commitments of roughly $1.3 billion as of mid-2025 across debt and equity platforms. CalSTRS uses external managers across public equity alongside a growing internal capability.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A large allocator with a formal emerging-manager program covering equities and a track record of external active-equity mandates. Its scale allows sizeable tickets once a firm clears diligence.
institutions.access_notes: Emerging-manager access is often intermediated through managers-of-managers and the public-equity consultant; direct mandates involve extensive staff and Investment Committee process.
institutions.tier_reason: Genuine emerging-manager and external-equity appetite, but competitive, consultant- and platform-mediated selection makes it a longer cycle than TRS Texas or Illinois.
sources: Diversity in the Management of Investments — CalSTRS — http://www.calstrs.com/diversity-in-the-management-of-investments
Investments — CalSTRS — http://www.calstrs.com/investments

institutions.name: State Board of Administration of Florida
institutions.strategy_fit: A very large external allocator whose global-equity portfolio is executed substantially through external active managers, offering meaningful ticket capacity.
institutions.description: The Florida SBA administers roughly $250 billion in total assets, of which the Florida Retirement System Pension Plan is the largest at around $205 billion. Global public equity is a core allocation implemented through numerous external managers alongside internal management. The SBA does not run a prominent named emerging-manager program and relies on consultants and rigorous internal diligence.
institutions.outreach_rationale: Scale and heavy external-equity usage mean large potential mandates, and the SBA periodically adds newer managers with differentiated processes. Best pursued once an institutional track record is established.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the global-equity team and the plan's investment consultants; there is no dedicated emerging-manager door, so entry is via standard searches.
institutions.tier_reason: Large external-equity allocator with real capacity, but no formal emerging-manager program and a conservative, consultant-driven selection process.
sources: State Board of Administration of Florida — https://www.sbafla.com/
Florida SBA Investments — https://www.sbafla.com/fsb/FRS-Pension-Plan

institutions.name: State of Wisconsin Investment Board
institutions.strategy_fit: A sophisticated allocator that blends internal and external public-equity management and continually evaluates specialist and newer external managers.
institutions.description: SWIB manages roughly $156 billion, principally for the Wisconsin Retirement System, using a mix of internal and external strategies across public and private markets. It maintains an extensive external-manager roster in public equity and is known for a rigorous, research-oriented selection process. SWIB does not operate a high-profile emerging-manager program but does add differentiated smaller managers.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A capable, well-resourced allocator that rewards clearly articulated investment edge and process, making it a credible target once a track record supports institutional diligence. External equity is a live allocation.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the public markets/external management team; expect deep quantitative and qualitative diligence and selective use of consultants.
institutions.tier_reason: Genuine external-equity appetite and analytical openness, but demanding diligence and no dedicated emerging-manager on-ramp.
sources: State of Wisconsin Investment Board (SWIB) — https://www.swib.state.wi.us/
SWIB How We Invest — https://www.swib.state.wi.us/how-we-invest

institutions.name: Virginia Retirement System
institutions.strategy_fit: Operates a Managed Allocation Portfolio (MAP) that seeds and incubates smaller and emerging external managers, including in public equity.
institutions.description: VRS manages roughly $115 billion and combines internal management with a broad external-manager roster. Its Managed Allocation Portfolio is designed to allocate to newer, smaller and emerging managers with the potential to graduate into the main program. VRS is regarded as a sophisticated, well-staffed plan that actively evaluates non-traditional managers.
institutions.outreach_rationale: The MAP structure is a purpose-built incubator for smaller managers, providing a concrete near-term entry point for an emerging equities firm. Graduation potential offers a growth path within the fund.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the internal investment staff responsible for the MAP; VRS conducts significant in-house diligence and uses consultants selectively.
institutions.tier_reason: Has an incubation vehicle for emerging managers, but access is staff-driven and selective rather than an open programmatic call.
sources: Virginia Retirement System — Investments — https://www.varetire.org/investments/
VRS Comprehensive Annual Financial Report — https://www.varetire.org/

institutions.name: Massachusetts Pension Reserves Investment Management Board
institutions.strategy_fit: PRIM's FUTURE Initiative is a dedicated emerging and diverse-manager program spanning public and private markets, aligned with a research-driven equities boutique.
institutions.description: PRIM manages the roughly $105 billion Massachusetts PRIT Fund almost entirely through external managers across public and private markets. Its FUTURE Initiative is a formal emerging/diverse-manager program with a multi-hundred-million-dollar allocation and a stated goal of increasing capital with smaller and diverse firms. PRIM is regarded as one of the more innovative and accessible large U.S. plans.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A fully externally managed fund with a named, well-resourced emerging-manager program and a reputation for engaging newer firms, making it a strong Tier 1/2 target. Public-equity mandates are core to the fund.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the FUTURE Initiative and public-markets investment team; PRIM uses general and specialist consultants and typically expects institutional operational infrastructure.
institutions.tier_reason: Strong appetite and a formal emerging-manager program, but a competitive, consultant-supported process and preference for demonstrable institutional readiness lengthen the cycle.
sources: Massachusetts PRIM Board — https://www.mapension.com/
PRIM FUTURE Initiative (emerging and diverse managers) — https://www.mapension.com/future-initiative/

institutions.name: Los Angeles County Employees Retirement Association
institutions.strategy_fit: Allocates public-equity mandates externally and has an emerging-manager and emerging-manager-of-managers consideration within its policy framework.
institutions.description: LACERA manages roughly $80 billion for Los Angeles County employees and invests substantially through external managers across asset classes. Its investment policy incorporates emerging-manager and diverse-manager objectives, and it has used emerging-manager-of-managers structures in public equity. Selection is board-governed and supported by asset-class consultants.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A large California allocator with an emerging-manager orientation and public-equity external mandates, offering a realistic path via managers-of-managers or direct search. Growing focus on manager diversity supports outreach.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the public-equity investment officers and the emerging-manager-of-managers platforms; board approval and consultant screening apply.
institutions.tier_reason: Emerging-manager objectives and external-equity usage, but access is consultant- and platform-mediated with board governance.
sources: Los Angeles County Employees Retirement Association (LACERA) — Investments — https://www.lacera.com/investments

institutions.name: University of Texas/Texas A&M Investment Management Company
institutions.strategy_fit: One of the largest endowment managers with substantial external public-equity and hedge-fund allocations and capacity for meaningful tickets.
institutions.description: UTIMCO manages roughly $77 billion for the University of Texas and Texas A&M systems, including the Permanent University Fund, making it the largest U.S. university-affiliated investor. It allocates heavily to external managers across global public equity, hedge funds and private markets. UTIMCO is a sophisticated, well-staffed office that periodically adds newer managers with differentiated edge.
institutions.outreach_rationale: Its scale allows sizeable allocations, and it maintains a large external public-equity and hedge-fund roster that occasionally welcomes emerging talent. A strong long-term target once a track record supports institutional diligence.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the public-markets/marketable alternatives team through referral; expect thorough diligence and a preference for demonstrable performance and infrastructure.
institutions.tier_reason: Large external-equity and hedge-fund allocator open to differentiated managers, but selective and referral-driven with no formal emerging-manager program.

UTIMCO Funds and Performance — https://www.utimco.org/funds/

institutions.name: Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System
institutions.strategy_fit: Allocates public-equity mandates to external managers and has historically supported emerging and diverse managers within its public-markets portfolio.
institutions.description: PSERS manages roughly $75 billion for Pennsylvania's public school employees and relies heavily on external managers across public and private markets. The system has maintained emerging- and diverse-manager considerations within its manager selection, though it does not run as prescriptive a program as Texas or Illinois. Manager hiring is board-governed and consultant-supported.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A sizeable external allocator with recurring public-equity searches and openness to smaller managers where performance and process are strong. Realistic once a defensible track record exists.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the public-markets investment team and the general investment consultant; expect board approval and formal search processes.
institutions.tier_reason: Active external-equity allocator with emerging-manager openness, but selection is consultant-gated and search-driven rather than programmatic.
sources: Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System (PSERS) — https://www.psers.pa.gov/

institutions.name: Connecticut Retirement Plans and Trust Funds
institutions.aka: CRPTF; Office of the Connecticut State Treasurer
institutions.strategy_fit: The Treasurer's Connecticut Inclusive Investment Initiative explicitly targets emerging and diverse managers across public-markets asset classes.
institutions.description: The Connecticut Retirement Plans and Trust Funds, overseen by the sole-fiduciary State Treasurer, manage roughly $55-60 billion and allocate substantially to external managers. The office runs the Connecticut Inclusive Investment Initiative (CIII), a formal commitment to increase allocations to emerging, diverse and Connecticut-based managers across public and private markets. Manager hiring is supported by asset-class consultants and the Investment Advisory Council.
institutions.outreach_rationale: A sole-fiduciary structure combined with a stated emerging/diverse-manager initiative makes decision-making comparatively direct and mission-aligned for a smaller firm. Public-equity mandates fall within scope.
institutions.access_notes: Engage the Pension Funds Management division and monitor the Treasurer's RFP calendar; the Investment Advisory Council reviews commitments and consultants play a screening role.
institutions.tier_reason: Formal inclusive-investment initiative with public-markets scope, but a mid-size fund with consultant screening and periodic search timing.
sources: Office of the Connecticut State Treasurer — Pension Funds Management — https://portal.ct.gov/ott/pension-funds/pension-fund-management
Connecticut Inclusive Investment Initiative — https://portal.ct.gov/ott

institutions.name: MIT Investment Management Company
institutions.strategy_fit: One of the more openly emerging-manager-friendly endowments, explicitly seeking to partner early with talented public-equity and other managers.
institutions.description: MITIMCo manages MIT's endowment of roughly $24.6 billion almost entirely through external managers. It is well known within the industry for actively seeking to back newer and smaller managers early, publishing guidance encouraging emerging managers to approach it. Its concentrated, long-horizon partnership model favors differentiated, research-driven firms.
institutions.outreach_rationale: MITIMCo's stated willingness to engage emerging managers directly makes it one of the most realistic endowment targets for a new equities boutique. Early backing from MIT is a powerful reference for further fundraising.
institutions.access_notes: MITIMCo accepts direct approaches from managers via its website and network; it does deep, patient diligence and values clear investment philosophy over AUM scale.
institutions.tier_reason: Endowment with an unusually explicit emerging-manager orientation and direct-access posture, though selective and long-horizon.

MITIMCo — Partnering with Managers — https://mitimco.org/managers/

institutions.name: University of Notre Dame Investment Office
institutions.strategy_fit: A fully externally managed endowment with a long record of backing emerging and boutique public-equity managers, including internationally.
institutions.description: The Notre Dame Investment Office manages an endowment of roughly $18 billion entirely through external managers across global public and private markets. It has a strong reputation for identifying and seeding smaller, high-conviction managers early in their lifecycle. The office is regarded as a sophisticated, relationship-driven allocator with global reach.
institutions.outreach_rationale: Notre Dame's willingness to partner with emerging managers and its global-equity focus make it a credible endowment target for a Hong Kong-based research-driven firm. An anchor relationship carries strong signaling value.
institutions.access_notes: Access is relationship- and referral-driven through the investment team; expect rigorous, long-horizon diligence and a preference for aligned, concentrated managers.
institutions.tier_reason: Endowment known for early manager backing and global equity, but access is network-driven and highly selective.
